prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1130; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a red signal in Baytown, Texas, when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of the stopped car. Driver 1 reported a wrist fracture and was transported for evaluation. Driver 2 stated that the vehicle slowed too late to avoid contact and that no other vehicles were involved. A Passenger was present in Driver 1's vehicle, but the officer could not confirm from statements alone which seat that person occupied at the moment of impact. Scene photographs confirm the general placement of both vehicles and the location of the rear-end damage. No independent witnesses were located. The visible damage to both vehicles is largely consistent with the reported speed and angle of impact. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the struck vehicle. The officer found no information indicating prior damage to either vehicle. It is not yet clear whether the wrist injury resulted from this collision, and the medical record has been requested for further review.
